item.title: New Best Start Family Hubs open across Cambridgeshire
item.description:
📰 FENLAND ANGELS RADIO | LOCAL NEWS
New Best Start Family Hubs open across Cambridgeshire
Cambridgeshire County Council has launched five new Best Start Family Hubs, including a site in Wisbech. These centres replace existing child and family facilities, bringing services like health, childcare, housing, and financial advice under one roof. While currently focused on support from pregnancy to age five, the service will eventually expand to assist young people up to age 19, or 25 for those with special educational needs.
The hubs are free to use and open to all families. Launch events are being held at each location throughout this week, offering residents the chance to meet staff and explore the available resources. Further information is also accessible through the council’s network of local sites and online services.

item.title: West Norfolk woman completes Ben Nevis climb for hospital unit
item.description:
📰 FENLAND ANGELS RADIO | LOCAL NEWS
West Norfolk woman completes Ben Nevis climb for hospital unit
A West Norfolk woman has raised over £540 for the Peddars Way end-of-life unit at the Queen Elizabeth Hospital in King’s Lynn. Jan Mick climbed Ben Nevis in memory of her father, Harry, who passed away earlier this month.
The challenge took nine hours and 20 minutes to complete, with Jan facing difficult conditions including strong winds, rain, and temperatures dropping to minus four degrees at the summit. Jan, who recently moved to the area from Hertfordshire, chose the climb to honour her father’s active lifestyle. The hospital has expressed its gratitude for the donation, which exceeded the original £200 target. Supporters can still contribute to the fundraiser online.
🔗 More details: https://www.lynnnews.co.uk/news/daughter-s-fundraising-climb-in-memory-of-dad-9484866/

item.title: Norfolk health officials consider future of A&E services
item.description:
📰 FENLAND ANGELS RADIO | LOCAL NEWS
Norfolk health officials consider future of A&E services
Health officials in Norfolk are considering plans that could see A&E units at the Queen Elizabeth Hospital in King’s Lynn and the James Paget Hospital in Gorleston closed. Confidential documents reveal three potential options for future emergency care, with only one retaining full A&E services at all three of the county’s hospitals. Other proposals include downgrading the units to urgent treatment centres or removing major trauma services.
The Norfolk and Waveney University Hospitals Group states that no final decisions have been made and that the documents are part of preliminary work. However, local MPs have expressed strong opposition to any potential downgrades, citing concerns over rural travel times and the impact on patient care.
🔗 More details: https://www.lynnnews.co.uk/news/norfolk-could-be-left-with-just-one-a-e-unit-amid-possible-c-9484716/

item.description:

Wisbech newsagent TG Jones to close in January
The newsagent and stationer TG Jones has confirmed it will shut its Wisbech branch early next year. The shop, located on the Market Place, is scheduled to close its doors on Saturday, January 9, 2027. The closure is part of a wider, court-approved restructuring plan affecting several of the company's stores across the UK.
A spokesperson for the retailer expressed regret over the impact on the local community and staff. A closing down sale will be held at the premises before the final closure date. The company stated that its current priority is supporting affected employees while continuing to serve customers during the final weeks of operation.

item.title: Three-year driving ban for holidaymaker caught in King’s Lynn
item.description:
📰 FENLAND ANGELS RADIO | LOCAL NEWS
Three-year driving ban for holidaymaker caught in King’s Lynn
A holidaymaker has been disqualified from driving for three years after being caught over the limit in King’s Lynn. Forty-two-year-old David Canatch, from Gainsborough, was stopped by police on Gayton Road after officers noticed his fog lights were on during clear weather. A breath test revealed he had 45 micrograms of alcohol per 100 millilitres of breath, exceeding the legal limit of 35.
Appearing at Lynn Magistrates’ Court on Thursday, Mr Canatch pleaded guilty to drink-driving. In addition to the driving ban, he was ordered to pay a £120 fine, a £48 victim surcharge, and £50 in court costs.

Opposition grows to Leverington asylum accommodation plans
Fenland District Council and North East Cambridgeshire MP Steve Barclay have voiced strong opposition to government plans for a 26-bed asylum seeker facility in Leverington. The Home Office proposal for Roman Court is intended to house mothers and babies as part of a wider move toward long-term dispersal accommodation.
However, local leaders have raised concerns regarding the suitability of the site and the potential for future changes to the facility's use. Mr Barclay has expressed fears that this is the first stage of a broader government policy to bring 205 asylum seekers into the district. No specific timeline for the project has been provided by the Home Office, which says it will continue to engage with local partners.

item.title: Improvement work begins at North Lynn ponds
item.description:
📰 FENLAND ANGELS RADIO | LOCAL NEWS
Improvement work begins at North Lynn ponds
Maintenance work is starting today at the Loke Road ponds in North Lynn. West Norfolk Council staff are clearing overhanging and diseased trees to improve the habitat for local fish and invertebrates. The project involves cutting back willow trees and removing two ash trees identified as diseased.
Officials say the work is necessary to prevent rotting leaves from depleting oxygen levels in the water and to reduce excessive shade. The clearance also aims to protect pond liners and dams from damage caused by aggressive willow roots. This initiative is part of a wider pond regeneration programme that began in 2023.

item.description:

Wisbech High Street redevelopment plans approved
Fenland District Council has approved plans to redevelop a vacant site on Wisbech High Street. The project will see the construction of commercial premises and six one-bedroom flats at numbers 11 and 12, with access provided via Castle Mews. The site has remained empty since the original Grade II listed buildings were demolished in 2020.
During a meeting on Wednesday, September 23, councillors described the two-decade delay in bringing the site back into use as embarrassing. Council leader Chris Boden has called for an explanation regarding previous administrative issues that stalled the development. Local representatives have welcomed the decision, noting that the project is a positive step for the town.

Wisbech academy hosts talks on the future of Fenland soil
The Green Skills Academy in Wisbech has hosted a collaborative session focused on the future of agriculture and peat soil in the Fens. The event brought together the Fenland Environmental Network and the non-profit group Fenland SOIL to discuss the long-term sustainability of the local landscape.
Organisers say the meeting provided a space for education providers and environmental groups to share expertise on land use and food production. The session aligns with the Cambridgeshire and Peterborough Local Skills Improvement Plan, which highlights sustainable land management as a priority for the region. The College of West Anglia says the initiative aims to help students gain the skills needed to support the local economy’s shift toward a more sustainable future.

item.description:

MP calls for Ely Junction upgrades to improve Fen Line services
South West Norfolk MP Terry Jermy is urging the Transport Secretary to prioritise upgrades to Ely Junction. Following a summer that saw hundreds of cancellations on the Fen Line, Mr Jermy met with the Fen Line Users’ Association to discuss the impact on passengers in King’s Lynn, Downham Market, and Watlington.
The MP highlighted issues including poor service reliability, cleanliness, and faulty air conditioning. While acknowledging that extreme weather has affected local peat soils, he argued that many delays remain avoidable. Mr Jermy is now pushing for the project to be included in the next government Spending Review to boost regional growth. Meanwhile, a new scheme launched on September 20 now allows passengers to use alternative operators if their train is cancelled.
